reviewers.persona: Kursleiterin DaF (A1.1): Natürlichkeit, Niveau, Didaktik, Szenenplausibilität

method: Both reviewers read every German string again: title and title.canDo, the start (7 Folge lines and the gist item), the 3 inputs (30 lines) and the flyer, 10 exam texts, 2 strategy cards, 8 redemittel, both speaking parts (cards, openingLine, hintWords, 16 model turns), the writing task (situation, 3 Leitpunkte, checklist, model), 4 check lines, the story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine and every explanation.de. We solved every item blind from promptDe plus its options, tiles or audio line: 1 start gist, 15 input items, 12 structuredInput, 33 authored pool items, 12 reserve, 10 exam items, 8 check items and 4 proof items. For sentence_building we permuted the tiles and checked every V2 and V1 order against accepted[]. For the generators we traced what the player builds: 3 × dictation.fromInput (6 sources, none with `say`), 3 × numbers.dictation, 2 × lex.articlePlural, 1 × lex.glossTyped and 3 × lex.glossMatch. Typed answers were graded as src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js grades them; it now folds German number words on every exact:number item. We confirmed in the player that non-exam options are shown in authored order: ItemView builds item.options and ChoiceList maps them unshuffled, and only zuordnen's right column is seeded. Exam blocks were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json: h1 is 6 × abc with 3 options, 2 plays and [32–53] words; h2 is 4 × R/F with 1 play and [29–47] words; sp2 has two topics with cards-ask; sp3 uses cards-request; s2 has 3 Leitpunkte and about 30 words. They were also checked against the rubric files (sd1-sp2, sd1-sp3, sd1-s2, course-micro and course-micro-sp all exist). Every exam text is original in the official format, and none copies a Modellsatz. We recomputed the word counts with the validator's wordCount: h1 50/41/37/41/37/38, h2 31/31/32/30, flyer 47, model text 26 (band 20–30) and cliffhanger 25. We ran the validator's own knownForms + licensedForms at a1.1-u04 over every German string of the unit (not only inputs and exam texts: prompts, options, instructions, titles, endLines and title.canDo) and looked up each unknown token's allocation in all eight lexicons. We read the u04 lexicon roles (16 productive / 16 receptive; the level profile's productiveShare is 0.5) against every production task and generator source. The grammar ceiling was checked with GRM-04 and grammar-spine.json. We read the can-dos against registries/cando/a1.json, the cast against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (Arjun's WG, and the ensemble genders -1/-2 f and -3/-4 m, which match every stem and explanation), and the story against the authored a1.1 units u01, u02, u07 and u08 (u03 is not on disk) and curriculum/a1-1.json u04/u05. We recomputed every sum: the market comes to 2,20 + 3,60 + 0,90 + 1,80 + 0,50 = 9,00 ✓, and the whole Saturday comes to 9,24 + 9,00 + 5,37 = 23,61 € plus 1,50 € Pfand out of the 50 € ✓. The Landeskunde claims (Sunday closure, Pfand) were read for currency from the reviewers' knowledge. The agent proxy blocks the source domains, so they could not be re-fetched in this session. Every r1, r2 and r3 finding was verified against the current file.

verdict: The unit's content is exit-grade: 0 BLOCKER and 0 MAJOR in the unit itself, and every criterion is at 4. We solved all 122 authored and proof items blind, and every key is right. No item is ambiguous or rejects a defensible answer, and ls2-i05 now accepts „neun“ (r3-F01 is closed, and the player also folds number words for every exact:number item). The German is correct and idiomatic on every model surface. du/Sie is right everywhere. H1, H2, Sp3 and S2 match sd1.json, the Sp2 round-2 topic now fits its questions, and the scenes, exam texts, check lines and cast agree with each other and with u01, u02, u07 and u08. Of the r3 findings, 4 are fixed, 1 is fixed with a side effect, and 2 are still open with other owners (the rule cards and the detectors). Two things still stop exit. (1) The validator run on this unit is red: the new LEX-07 rail finds 20 example sentences above their unit's grammar ceiling in the shared a1.1 lexicon, all in other units' entries (F01, lexicon owner and spine owner; nothing to change in u04). (2) Seven minors are logged, where exit allows five. Four of them come from rails the rule-smith added today, which the unit meets for the first time. Production drills and generators are built on receptive lemmas, including a scored Check item (F02). Non-exam keys sit at b in 19 of 33 items and in 5 of 6 in the Check (F03). Role nouns such as Verkäufer and Prospekt are unglossed or unallocated on task surfaces (F04, the r3-F05 class recurring). The Landeskunde claims have no facts[] record, and the flyer omits the Pfand on a milk bottle that has carried one since 2024 (F05). F03, F05, F06 and the unit parts of F02 and F04 are data edits in the unit. After them the unit carries 3 owner-held minors (F04 lexicon allocation, F07, F08) and exits as soon as LEX-07 is green.

findings.quote: flyer „Milch, 1 Flasche: nur 0,99 Euro“ directly above „Wasser, 6 Flaschen: nur 2,49 Euro plus Pfand“ · gloss Pfand 'deposit (on bottles)' · ls3-l11 „Morgen ist Sonntag, da sind die Supermärkte in Deutschland zu.“ · "facts": [] · validator „CON-06 skipped: no facts[] records in the target“
findings.problem: The unit's texts carry the plan's two Landeskunde points (curriculum/a1-1.json u04: „sonntags meist geschlossen, Flaschenpfand in Deutschland“) as claims, but the unit has no facts[] record. SCHEMA §3.4 requires a Fact for every factual claim, and CON-06 therefore skips the unit. So nobody has checked the claims for currency and exceptions, which the §9.5 brief requires. (1) Pfand: the flyer marks the deposit on the water but not on the milk, which it sells by the bottle, and the unit's own gloss ties Pfand to bottles. Since 1 January 2024 the single-use deposit (0,25 €) also covers milk in plastic bottles (VerpackG § 31; the transition for milk drinks has ended), and glass milk bottles are Mehrweg with a deposit of their own. The flyer's contrast therefore teaches that a milk bottle has no Pfand, which is out of date. (2) Sunday: „die Supermärkte in Deutschland“ is stated without exception. The plan's own word is „meist“, and a newcomer in Leipzig will meet supermarkets open on Sunday in the main station, at petrol stations, on the few verkaufsoffene Sonntage and, in some Länder, as unstaffed digital mini-markets.
findings.fix: Flyer: „Milch, 1 Flasche: nur 0,99 Euro plus Pfand“ (every sum in the unit stays the same, because Pfand is added on top). Add facts a1.1-u04-f01 (Pfand: single-use 0,25 € on water and, since 2024, on milk in plastic bottles; Mehrweg glass with its own deposit) and a1.1-u04-f02 (shops are closed on Sunday under the Länder's Ladenöffnungsgesetze; exceptions: stations, airports, petrol stations, a few verkaufsoffene Sonntage a year). Each record needs sources (gesetze-im-internet.de VerpackG § 31; SächsLadÖffG), factsCheckedOn, currentAsOf and exceptions. The agent proxy blocks these domains, so this review could not re-read them: the author verifies them before setting verification 'verified'. Optionally soften ls3-l11 to „da sind die Supermärkte hier zu“.
findings.proposedRule: CON-06: do not skip a unit whose curriculum entry names a `landeskunde` point, or whose lines state a country-wide rule („in Deutschland“, „in Österreich“, „in der Schweiz“). Such a unit needs ≥ 1 facts[] record or a deviation.reason. Failing fixture: a1.1-u04 with facts []. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: rc.artikel-genus-plural „Unbestimmt heißt es ein (der, das) und eine (die).“ · table row „unbestimmt | ein Apfel | ein Brot | eine Tomate“ · rc.moechte „Mit einem zweiten Verb steht der Infinitiv am Ende: Ich möchte bezahlen.“
findings.problem: r2-F09 and r3-F06 are still open, and both cards are byte-identical to r3. The indefinite-article rule and its unlabeled table row hold only for the nominative. Yet this unit's frames are accusative (brauchen, möchte, kaufen), and its chunk is „Ich möchte einen Apfel“, so a learner who applies the card writes ✗„Wir brauchen ein Käse / Ich möchte ein Apfel“, which u06 has to unteach (§9.5: a simplification that has become false in context). rc.moechte previews the Satzklammer (g.koennen, a1.1-u08) with bezahlen (a1.1-u09), a rule that no line, item or task of u04 practises.
findings.fix: Rule-cards owner: label the row „unbestimmt (Nominativ)“ and add „Achtung: Ich möchte einen Apfel. (der → einen, Einheit 6)“. In rc.moechte, replace the infinitive sentence with „Ich möchte ein Kilo Tomaten, bitte.“ or move it to depth 2. Both cards stay within ruleCardMaxWords 60.

Rule-smith: add the möchte paradigm to the Nullartikel detector's stoplist and „macht (das) zusammen“ to the separable-verb detector's. Suppress an advisory whose construction is licensed as a chunk at the position.
